question.text: Among alkali metal salts, the lithium salts are the poorest conductors of electricity in aqueous solution because of

options.text: lower ability of  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>  ions to polarize water molecules
higher degree of hydration of  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>  ions

solution.text: Ionic conductance in solution depends upon the mobility of ions, which depend upon the degree (or extent) of hydration. Since charge/radius ratio is maximum for  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> , so it is hydrated to a maximum extent. Thus, the ionic size in aqueous solution, instead of increasing, actually decreases on moving from  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>  to  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> .
